description: Conformance rules for OpenSpecLib Format v1 (docs/spec/format-v1.md section 8). Normative. `level`: 'must' rules decide conformance; 'should' rules are recommendations reported as warnings; 'qa' rules belong to the OpenSpecLib quality profile. `applies_to`: 'collection' or 'index' files.

rules.title: Footer metadata
rules.text: The file is a valid Parquet file. The footer key `openspeclib` exists, holds valid JSON that validates against `#/$defs/collectionFooter` in the footer schema, `format_version` has major version 1, and `created` is a real calendar date-time. The file does not also carry the key `openspeclib_index`.

rules.title: Core columns
rules.text: Every core column exists with its type, as implied by the Parquet logical type and repetition (`ARROW:schema` hints such as dictionary encoding, fixed_size_list and large/view variants do not change it; list child names and nullability are not significant; date64 equals date32; 2-level list encodings are accepted; an all-null nullable column may use the Arrow `null` type). Columns marked non-nullable contain no nulls. `id`, `collection`, `original_id`, `name`, `material_name`, `license` and non-null `dataset_id` contain no empty or whitespace-only strings. List columns of strings contain no null elements.

rules.title: No unknown columns
rules.text: Every column is a core column, a column of a declared extension, `extra`, or starts with `x_`. Columns starting with `x_` are flat: primitive types or lists of primitive types, no structs or maps.

rules.title: Extension column types
rules.text: Every extension column, and `extra`, has its defined Arrow type, and each non-null `extra` value is a JSON object.

rules.title: Identifiers
rules.text: `id` is unique within the file and matches `^{collection}:[A-Za-z0-9._~-]{1,200}$`, where `{collection}` is the footer `collection.id`.

rules.title: Collection column
rules.text: `collection` equals the footer `collection.id` on every row.

rules.title: Vocabularies
rules.text: `material_category`, `quantity`, `geometry` and `wavelength_unit` hold values from their vocabularies.

rules.title: Wavelength axis
rules.text: `wavelengths` has at least 2 elements, no nulls, all finite and greater than 0, and is strictly increasing or strictly decreasing.

rules.title: Values
rules.text: `values` has the same length as `wavelengths`. Its elements are finite or NaN: no nulls, no infinities, and no finite value with magnitude above 1e10.

rules.title: Wavelength extent in nm
rules.text: `wavelength_min_nm` and `wavelength_max_nm` equal the minimum and maximum of `wavelengths` converted to nanometres: |a − b| ≤ 1e-6 · max(|a|, |b|).

rules.title: Licences
rules.text: Every non-empty licence field (the per-row `license` column, footer `collection.license`, and each `datasets.*.license`) is an SPDX license expression, a `LicenseRef-` identifier defined in `collection.license_refs`, or `NOASSERTION` on its own. Operators (AND, OR, WITH) are upper case. Validators check expression syntax and `LicenseRef-` definitions, not the SPDX licence list. Tokens are separated by single spaces or parentheses; no leading or trailing whitespace; no `DocumentRef-`.

rules.title: Dataset references
rules.text: Every non-null `dataset_id` is a key of the footer `datasets` object, and every key of `datasets` is the `dataset_id` of at least one row. Where a dataset gives `spectra_included`, it equals the number of rows with that `dataset_id`.

rules.title: Per-band arrays
rules.text: `bandpass_fwhm` and `values_stddev`, where present and not null, have the same length as `wavelengths`; their elements are finite and non-negative, or NaN.

rules.title: Index file
rules.text: The file is a valid Parquet file whose footer key `openspeclib_index` validates against `#/$defs/indexFooter`, and which does not also carry `openspeclib`. It meets every requirement of spec section 7: required columns with correct types and no others except `x_`; `file` values are relative paths or http(s) URLs listed in the footer, each file listed once; `id` unique across the index; every row matches exactly one row of its file with equal shared values (`x_` columns not compared; extension columns a file lacks are null); every row of each listed file appears exactly once; `num_spectra`, `metadata` and `sha256` match.

rules.title: Sorted with statistics
rules.text: Rows are sorted by `id` in ascending byte (UTF-8 code unit) order, and Parquet statistics are written for `id`. Files with no rows are exempt.

rules.title: Row group size
rules.text: Row groups hold at most 250 spectra.

rules.title: Array encoding
rules.text: `values`, `wavelengths`, `bandpass_fwhm` and `values_stddev` use BYTE_STREAM_SPLIT encoding on their leaf columns, without dictionary encoding, compressed with zstd.

rules.title: Non-empty spectra
rules.text: Every spectrum has at least one non-NaN value.

rules.title: Known geometry
rules.text: At most half of the spectra have `geometry` = `unknown`.

rules.title: Value scale
rules.text: The median of a spectrum's valid values (finite, not a sentinel) lies inside the hard bounds for its quantity. The median may be approximate.

rules.title: Value bounds
rules.text: No valid value lies outside the hard bounds for its quantity. Not reported for spectra that fail Q1.

rules.title: Suspect values
rules.text: Valid values outside the warning bounds are reported as warnings. Not reported for spectra that fail Q1 or Q2.

rules.title: Plausible wavelength extent
rules.text: `wavelength_min_nm` is at least 100 and `wavelength_max_nm` at most 1,000,000 (100 nm to 1 mm). An extent outside this range almost always means a mislabelled `wavelength_unit`.
